venue.name: Mount Washington Alpine Resort
venue.description: Mount Washington Alpine Resort sits in the mountains above the Comox Valley, about 30 minutes north of Courtenay by road. In winter it runs alpine and Nordic skiing, snowshoeing, fat biking and a tube park, with published school group packages that need a minimum booking of 15 and a separate community and youth group rate that needs 20. In summer it runs a scenic chairlift, a lift served bike park, hiking trails, disc golf and a guided zipline. Age and height rules are set activity by activity rather than across the whole resort.

facility_notes.washrooms: Washrooms are available in the ZipTour Centre

restrictions: All vehicles on the Strathcona Parkway must be equipped with good winter tires and carry chains, ready to use when the chain-up light is on
Dogs are not allowed to ride the chairlift
Children in backpacks and newborns in slings are not permitted on the chairlift
Ski or hard-shell boots are not permitted in the Tube Park
No sleds, toboggans or self-owned tubes are permitted in the Tube Park
venue.hours_notes: Hours change by season and by activity. When this was checked the resort was closed midweek, with the Bike Park and ZipTour running at weekends only through September.
venue.seasonal_notes: The Tube Park was closed for the rest of the 2025/26 season when this was checked and tickets for 26/27 were not on sale. Winter 26/27 lesson programming had also not been announced. Bear's Den Daycare runs weekends from June 27 to September 6.
venue.price_year_or_season: School and community group rates are posted for the coming winter on pages updated in August 2026. ZipTour, scenic chairlift and summer camp prices are for summer 2026.

programs.name: Full Day Alpine Session Package for school groups
programs.description: A full day of alpine skiing or snowboarding for a class at $99, taking in a full day lesson, a full day lift ticket and equipment rentals. Mornings are skill building and afternoons are guided riding around the mountain with the same instructor. The minimum booking size for school groups is 15 and lessons are mandatory for all educational school groups. The resort says GPS trackers will be given to every student this season.
programs.what_children_do: Ski or ride with one instructor for the whole day, working on technique in the morning and then following that instructor around the mountain in the afternoon.
programs.our_note: This is a whole day on snow plus roughly an hour of mountain road each way from the Comox Valley, so it is a long day for younger children. They will put a bus on from the Comox Valley for $650 return if you would rather not drive.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site and there are cafes and a cafeteria, but nothing is published about a room a class can eat a packed lunch in, or about where a bus parks. Ask about both, and note that vehicles need good winter tires and chains on the parkway.
programs.extra_fees_note: A return bus within the Comox Valley can be added for $650.
programs.evidence: Minimum booking size for school groups: 15.

programs.name: Alpine Educational Groups Program
programs.description: The traditional school group option at $89, taking in a 1.5 hour skiing or snowboarding lesson, a lift ticket and equipment rentals. The minimum booking size for school groups is 15 and lessons are mandatory for all educational school groups.
programs.what_children_do: Take a ninety minute skiing or snowboarding lesson in a small class, then use the lift ticket for the rest of the time on the hill.
programs.our_note: Ninety minutes on the snow plus the drive still eats a full school day once you count boots and bathroom stops. If you want the children out longer, the full day package is only ten dollars more.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site and there are cafes and a cafeteria, but nothing is published about a room a class can eat a packed lunch in, or about where a bus parks. Ask about both, and note that vehicles need good winter tires and chains on the parkway.
programs.evidence: Alpine Skiing & Snowboarding: a 1.5-hour lesson*, lift ticket, and equipment rentals.

programs.name: Local school day trip for Courtenay and Campbell River schools
programs.description: A heavily discounted day trip for School District 71 and 72 schools, from $29 a person at Nordic and $39 a person at Alpine, built to fit inside the school day. Chaperone tickets are free at one per ten students, and a return bus within the Comox Valley can be added for $650. Lessons are mandatory for all educational school groups.
programs.what_children_do: Cross country ski on the Nordic trails or ski and ride on the alpine slopes, with a lesson as part of the package.
programs.our_note: If you teach in School District 71 or 72 this is by far the cheapest way onto the mountain, and it is built to fit the school day rather than run past the bell. Nordic is ten dollars less a head and gentler for a first time group.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site and there are cafes and a cafeteria, but nothing is published about a room a class can eat a packed lunch in, or about where a bus parks. Ask about both, and note that vehicles need good winter tires and chains on the parkway.
programs.extra_fees_note: Alpine is $39 a person against $29 at Nordic. A return bus within the Comox Valley can be added for $650.
programs.evidence: We continue offering our local schools trips to Mount Washington for as little as $29 per person at Nordic and $39 at Alpine.

programs.name: Community Groups Special beginner session
programs.description: A $29.95 a person late afternoon session for youth organisations, schools and non profit groups, taking in a beginner lesson, gear rental and a lift ticket. It runs Thursday to Saturday from 4pm to 6pm or 5pm to 6pm. The minimum size for community and youth groups is 20. The offer is limited to beginner lessons, though lift ticket and rental only options are also available.
programs.what_children_do: Take a beginner skiing or snowboarding lesson in the late afternoon, in rented gear, on the learning terrain.
programs.our_note: Twenty is the floor for a community group, which is a lot for a small daycare. It is also a late finish and a dark drive down the mountain in midwinter, so think about pickup times before you commit.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site and there are cafes and a cafeteria, but nothing is published about a room a class can eat a packed lunch in, or about where a bus parks. Ask about both, and note that vehicles need good winter tires and chains on the parkway.
programs.evidence: We are excited to announce a new feature this year – our $29.95 Community Groups special!

programs.name: Snow School group lesson
programs.description: Group lessons at the Snow School, kept small and sorted by ability. They run 2.5 hours for Tot and Child aged 4 to 7 and 2 hours for Youth aged 13 to 18 and Adult 19 and over. Prices and dates for the 26/27 winter had not been published when this was checked.
programs.what_children_do: Learn to ski or snowboard in a small class with an instructor, on beginner terrain.
programs.our_note: Four is the youngest they take in a group lesson, which is the real floor for a preschool group on the snow. Nothing was priced for the coming winter when we looked, so you will have to ask.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site and there are cafes and a cafeteria, but nothing is published about a room a class can eat a packed lunch in, or about where a bus parks. Ask about both, and note that vehicles need good winter tires and chains on the parkway.
programs.evidence: All group lessons are 2.5 hours in length for Tot & Child (4 to 7) and 2 hours in length for Youth

programs.name: Tube Park session
programs.description: A one hour pass on the tube park lanes, with a covered surface lift carrying riders back to the top. Every rider needs a ticket whatever their age or height and must be at least 2 years old, and riders must be at least 42 inches, or 107 cm, tall to have their own tube. Anyone under 42 inches rides free in an adult's tube, and children under 12 must be with an adult unless they are tall enough to ride alone. Ski or hard shell boots are not allowed, and no sleds, toboggans or personal tubes are permitted.
programs.what_children_do: Slide down a groomed lane in a tube, then ride the covered lift back to the top and go again, in squares of up to four tubes.
programs.our_note: The height rule bites harder than the age rule. A four or five year old under 42 inches can only ride in an adult's tube, so count your adults before you count your children. There is also straw on the lanes at times to slow the tubes, which matters if anyone in the group reacts to it.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site. The park was shut for the rest of the season when this was checked and no price was up for the coming winter, so you cannot budget this one yet.
programs.evidence: All riders must have a ticket regardless of age or height, and be at least 2 years of age.

programs.name: Summer scenic chairlift ride
programs.description: A ride up the Eagle Express for views over the Salish Sea and Strathcona Provincial Park, with the option to get off at the peak and walk around before riding back down. Children must be 3 or older to ride and children under 3 are not allowed. Children in backpacks and newborns in slings are not permitted, and dogs cannot ride. If you hike up the trails, the ride down is free.
programs.what_children_do: Sit on a chairlift for the ride up, walk around the mountain top, then ride back down or walk down the trail.
programs.our_note: Three is the hard floor here and there is no way round it, since babies in carriers and slings are not allowed on the chair either. When we checked, summer tickets were only being sold at the kiosk or over the phone, so do not plan on booking online.
programs.practical_summary: This one is outdoors at altitude with no rain plan published. Nothing is stated about washrooms at the top or where a bus parks, so ask when you phone the ticket line.
programs.extra_fees_note: Tots aged 3 to 6 ride free. Child 7 to 12 and Youth 13 to 18 are $15, Adult 19 to 64 is $20 and Senior 65 and over is $15. A Scenic 4Pak for any group of four is $60 with extra people at $15. On Family Fridays from 3:30pm to 7:30pm children 7 to 12 are $5 and youth are $10.
programs.evidence: Children must be 3+ years of age to ride the chairlift; children under 3 are not allowed on the chairlift.

programs.name: Eagle's Flight ZipTour
programs.description: A guided zipline tour over four spans totalling 2.3 km, with a shorter Hawk Flight half tour starting from the third line. Riders must weigh between 50 and 260 lbs and be between 4 feet and 6 feet 8 inches tall, and heights and weights are measured at check in. Riders must be 10 or older, and anyone aged 10 to 15 must be accompanied on the tour by a parent or guardian aged 19 or older. Each tour needs at least 4 people. Allow up to 3 hours and arrive 30 minutes early. The half tour is $44 for ages 16 and under and $59 for 16 and over.
programs.what_children_do: Carry an 18 lb trolley in a backpack up several flights of stairs and along some hiking, then ride four ziplines controlling their own speed.
programs.our_note: The rule that stops most school groups is that every rider aged 10 to 15 needs a parent or guardian aged 19 or older with them on the tour, not just a teacher waiting at the bottom. Sort that out before you book anything else. It is also three hours of stairs and pack carrying, so it is not a gentle outing.
programs.practical_summary: There are washrooms in the ZipTour Centre and some first come lockers on the Marmots floor. It runs outdoors and is cancelled in lightning, high wind, low visibility or heavy rain, so build in a fallback.
programs.payment_timing: The full amount of the reservation must be paid in full at the time of booking.
programs.cancellation_note: Cancel 48 hours or more before the tour for a full refund or a reschedule. Between 24 and 47 hours before, you can reschedule but there is no refund. Under 24 hours, or no notice at all, means you lose the payment and the chance to reschedule.
programs.evidence: Guests must be ten years of age or older and guests between the ages of 10 and 15 (inclusive) must have a parent/guardian

programs.name: Groms Guided Ride in the Bike Park
programs.description: A two hour guided ride in the Bike Park for riders aged 6 to 12, in groups of no more than six with a guide who specialises in working with children, on green, blue and lighter black trails with priority lift loading. The $34 price is for the guiding only. Lift tickets and rentals must be bought as add ons and no rental discounts apply. Sessions run Saturday and Sunday at noon and 2:30pm. The resort recommends the Learn to Ride and Step Up lessons first for anyone new to mountain biking.
programs.what_children_do: Ride downhill trails in the Bike Park behind a guide for two hours, loading the chairlift ahead of the queue between runs.
programs.our_note: Six riders per guide is a hard cap, so a class needs several sessions and several guides booked at once. The price is for the guide only, so a bike, armour and a lift ticket all land on top of it.
programs.practical_summary: Outdoors in the Bike Park with no wet weather alternative published. Washrooms are on site, but lunch space and bus parking are not stated.
programs.extra_fees_note: Tickets and rentals are not included in the price of the lesson and must be purchased as add-ons.
programs.evidence: our Groms Guided Ride is the ultimate experience for young riders aged 6–12

gaps: AGE AND HEIGHT MINIMUMS ARE PER ACTIVITY, NOT PER RESORT. Tube Park: at least 2 years old, and at least 42 inches (107 cm) tall to have your own tube; under 42 inches rides free in an adult's tube; under 12 must be with an adult unless tall enough to ride alone. Summer scenic chairlift: 3 or older, under 3 not allowed, no children in backpacks and no newborns in slings. Snow School group lessons: Tot and Child band starts at 4. ZipTour: 10 or older, plus 50 to 260 lbs and 4 feet to 6 feet 8 inches, and riders aged 10 to 15 need a parent or guardian aged 19 or older on the tour. Groms Guided Ride in the Bike Park: 6 to 12. Learn to Ride and Step Up bike lessons: child band 7 to 12. Bear's Den Daycare: 18 months to 5 years. No age minimum at all is published for the school group ski packages.

PER PERSON INFERENCE: the $99 full day package and the $89 educational groups program are not labelled per person or per group on the page. We have recorded both per child because the local schools line beside them says 'as little as $29 per person', and because each package includes an individual lift ticket, rental and lesson. If $99 were the price for a whole group of 15 the difference would be $99 against about $1,485, so confirm it in writing before you budget.
The $29.95 community and youth group rate is stated per person on the page, so that one is not an inference.
Free chaperone tickets at one per ten students are listed only under the local School District 71 and 72 offer, not under the $99 or $89 packages. Whether adults are free on those two is not stated.
No months are published for any of the winter group packages, so which months they actually run is unknown.
No months are published for the summer scenic chairlift or the Bike Park guided rides either, so the season dates for those are unknown.
No adult to child ratio is published for any activity except the Tube Park rule that children under 12 need an adult with them.
No minimum booking notice is published for school or community groups. The contact page gives notice periods for individual lessons only, and gives two different ones.

Winter 26/27 prices for Snow School group lessons and Tube Park tickets were not published when this was checked. The group lessons page said only that news about winter 26/27 programming was still to come.

RETRIEVAL NOTE: every email address on this site is hidden behind Cloudflare email protection and comes back as an unreadable link to a plain fetch. Opened in a browser they decode to ski@mountwashington.ca for general and group enquiries, ziptour@mountwashington.ca for the zipline, bikereservation@mountwashington.ca for bike park lessons and summercamps@mountwashington.ca for the summer camps. A fetch-only re-run will appear to find no email addresses at all.

COORDINATES: the resort publishes a street address of #1 Strathcona Parkway but no coordinates for itself. The map links on the Getting Here page are Comox Valley bus pick-up points, not the resort. The point recorded here is the centre of the resort's own mapped ski area, which sits roughly a kilometre from the Alpine Lodge where a group would actually meet, so do not route a bus to it without checking.

Whether a school group has anywhere indoors to eat a packed lunch is not stated. There are several cafes, a cafeteria and restaurants, and catering is offered to groups, but no lunch room is described.
Bus parking is not addressed. The resort offers a $650 return bus from the Comox Valley and a third party shuttle service, but says nothing about where a school bus drops off or parks.
Wheelchair access, stroller access and a wet weather alternative are not addressed anywhere for group visits.

The summer day camps are sold as individual weekly registrations rather than group bookings, so they are not listed as programs here. For reference, the Alpine Adventure Camp takes ages 5 to 12 at $249 a week, the Bike Adventure Camp takes ages 7 to 12 at $279 a week, both 9am to 4pm with a packed lunch, and a shuttle from Courtenay or Comox is $99 a camp week. Almost every 2026 week was sold out when this was checked.

Bear's Den Daycare is supervised drop-in childcare for tots aged 18 months to 5 years while parents are on the mountain, not a group booking. Its licence limits any one child to four days a calendar month, and parents must bring proof of medical coverage and immunisation history.

CATEGORY NOTE: filed under community and civic because the recreation category no longer exists. The summer side of this venue, the hiking trails, alpine wildflowers and the marmot tours, is genuinely nature based and might sit better under nature and outdoors.

IMAGE NOTE: the two banner photographs used here carry no alt attribute on the site, so their alt text was written after opening the image files and looking at them. The other three carry the site's own alt text.

RETRIEVAL NOTE: the ZipTour price table, its weight, height and age rules and the whole ZipTour FAQ sit inside collapsed accordions that a plain fetch does render but a browser hides until they are opened. They were expanded and read from the live page, and the prices there match: $74 for ages 10 to 15 and $99 for 16 and over on the full tour, $44 and $59 on the half tour.

conflicts.note: Their contact page gives two different notice periods for booking a lesson. One line says 48 hours ahead, another says 24 hours through the call centre with a cut off at noon the day before. Book as early as you can and get the date confirmed.
